Mavis and Carole have lived in this gracious and welcoming 2 story Queen Anne home since 1986, and have furnished it to reflect our love of art, books, music and comfort. It is designed for socializing, relaxing and enjoying a view that still makes us pinch ourselves from time to time.
Mavis was raised in Atlanta, Georgia in a family of art and music lovers. After a fulfilling career as a Psychotherapist, she now spends her time traveling, enjoying mostly classical performing arts in San Francisco and in Manhattan, where we have a tiny studio pied-a-terre. Her only regrets about being away from San Francisco are missing our amazing neighbors, and not being able to play her Vintage Mason & Hamlin Baby Grand Piano.
Carole grew up in California and then moved with her family to Memphis, TN. She was able return to Northern California to attend Mills College. Now happily retired from real estate finance, she spends her time cooking, entertaining and planning trips. Like Mavis, she is crazy about New York, and would happily live at Lincoln Center. (Well, Broadway, too.)
Mavis and Carole have swapped houses in Barcelona, Sitges, Berlin, Paris, and Dully, Switzerland (near Lake Geneva.) Our home has gotten wonderful reviews and we have made friends with several of our fellow swappers. 
We love our home, our neighborhood, and our beautiful city by the bay. We look forward to sharing them with our guests.

Haight-Ashbury is an incredible relic of San Francisco’s past. The neighborhood, also known as “The Haight” or “Upper Haight”, succinctly personifies the City’s history, aesthetic, and culture.

It is perhaps the most colorful swath of acreage in San Francisco, and remains one of the last-standing neighborhoods to retain an eccentric personality.

The Haight rose to fame during the Counterculture Movement during the Vietnam War era; it became a regular feature in international news headlines and incited a global initiative for social change with special thanks to the 1967 Summer of Love, and a little help from Janis Joplin and the Grateful Dead.

The Haight-Ashbury neighborhood is nestled in between three parks: Golden Gate Park, the Panhandle, and Buena Vista Park, making it somewhat of an urban oasis. Within the parks you'll find: Museums, botanical gardens, seasonal music festivals, and a tea garden.

neighborhood_overview:
We are located in the heart of Telegraph Hill, a quintessential San Francisco neighborhood. Perhaps most famous for its Coit Tower, Telegraph Hill rises steeply out of North Beach and descends dramatically down to the Embarcadero. Each day hundreds of tourists climb Coit Tower’s 200 steps to take in an awe-inspiring 360-degree view of San Francisco and the greater Bay Area.

Telegraph Hill is famous for the Filbert Street Steps - a beautiful pedestrian walkway that extends from Coit Tower down to Kearney Street at the edge of The Embarcadero. The Filbert steps leads walkers along a secluded path alongside charming gardens that belong to Telegraph Hill residents. The steps provide a great opportunity to catch a glimpse of the famous Telegraph Hill parrots. These beautiful bright green tropical birds are members of a greater colony of feral parrots that live at various locations throughout San Francisco.

Haight-Ashbury is an incredible relic of San Francisco’s past. The neighborhood, also known as “The Haight” or “Upper Haight”, succinctly personifies the City’s history, aesthetic, and culture.

It is perhaps the most colorful swath of acreage in San Francisco, and remains one of the last-standing neighborhoods to retain an eccentric personality.

The Haight rose to fame during the Counterculture Movement during the Vietnam War era; it became a regular feature in international news headlines and incited a global initiative for social change with special thanks to the 1967 Summer of Love, and a little help from Janis Joplin and the Grateful Dead.

The Haight-Ashbury neighborhood is nestled in between three parks: Golden Gate Park, the Panhandle, and Buena Vista Park, making it somewhat of an urban oasis. Within the parks you'll find: Museums, botanical gardens, seasonal music festivals, and a tea garden.

host_about:
There's one word that fully encompasses the experience of staying at our hostel: Community. At first glance, one might presume that the endgame of all hostels is to create a sense of firm familiarity among guest and staff alike, but with us, you can feel it. With a full roster of events that are ongoing, all inclusive in both experience and price, and a design purposefully conducive to the gathering of folks all around the world, we are dedicated to establishing a world reaching community that you feel while you are here, and long after your stay.

Our adventure travel company launched in 1974 with the purpose of bringing together folks who share the same single ambition: Travel! For the next twenty years, our buses brought these wandering souls to experience places as close as Santa Barbara and Monterey, to destinations as far as Alaska, New York City, and even Costa Rica. As incredible as these destinations are, we believe it is more about the journey than the destination.  

In the 1990’s we opened our San Francisco hostel to offer a haven for travelers to settle, rest, and of course party! In opening our hostel, we hoped to create a sense of community and create a haven where these newly found friendships would flourish.  We believe that bringing people together to create a community is the true purpose of a hostel.

Community. That’s what we’re about.  Stop by and experience it for yourself.

Please contact us to confirm the exact availability of the apartment you are interested in. We’d love to host you (and your family) for your vacation or business trip.

neighborhood_overview: Excelsior is a wonderful neighborhood with an eclectic mix of people. Locals in the area have also typically been here for a long time, so the area is loved and cared for. We get tons of sun, and Excelsior is one of the warmer and least-foggy districts in SF. host_about:
'Not all who wander are lost.' I love this quote. 
I am that wanderer, incredibly lucky to be infected with the passion and audacity to travel often and solo. 
I was born and raised in San Francisco. I am a native. I love my city. I’ve watched it evolve. But I have also left it many times in my youth. I’ve left it to study abroad in France. Best decision of my college life! I backpacked solo around western Europe. 
I’ve left SF when I was a member of the Armed Forces and was stationed around our country. I’ve also driven as far north as Niagara Falls and over to the Canadian side. 
Career wise, I’ve spent a decade working in property management and rentals. As a hobby, I write 90-minutes every morning at dawn, six-days a week. 
I am cursed with this blessing of being unceasingly interested in people. I love meeting people. I love hearing stories. And I love writing them. 
As I review my life’s experiences, I’ve come upon one very simple realization, that proclaimed secret of success. It is merely this: ‘Say what you will do and do what you will say.’
The prolific Seth Godin, talented blogger said creativity isn’t the most important part. What counts is being able to ship! Ship on time. And ship again. And again. And again.

neighborhood_overview:
The Bayview is located on the South East portion of San Francisco, or as I like to call it, the Lower East Side of SF (it will catch on). It truly is a gem of a neighborhood that is culturally and socio-economically diverse, and one of the last ones in SF with a great mix of natives, artists and newcomers to the city. While I have not lived in this neighborhood that long, moved here in 2017, I am constantly reminded of what a great decision it was to move here. Lots of fun being part of a neighborhood in transition, with new and places popping up.

Though this neighborhood is residential, public transportation is pretty easy, and there's plenty of parking all around. There's also a few breweries, bakeries, a mead company and a lot more to offer.

When staying with us, you'll meet like-minded individuals with a culture of pragmatic cooperation and collaboration. We are more than just about housing. We care, build trusted relationships, and support each other in achieving our goals and startup visions. 

We offer private and shared bedrooms that allow even bootstrapping founders to live in a great neighborhood and the friendly, clean, convenient, and safe place they deserve. 

We partner with startup accelerators, bootcamps, coding academies, and co-working spaces and prefer recruiting our residents through peer-recommendations and our networks. So please let us know how you have heard from us.

I am also an entrepreneur and builder who now runs an international startup accelerator out of Palo Alto, SF, and NYC. When I bring founders from abroad, one of the hardest challenges for them is to find appropriate housing. That's why I stepped up and created Bed|n|Build.

We love social, easy going, and low maintenance folks. After all, it's a co-living place with diverse people from the different corners of this world. Nerdy - sure. Geeky - also welcome. 

Don't reach out if others have described you as picky, high maintenance, or a drama king or queen. Also, do not contact us if you are not interested in getting to know the other builders sharing the house or joining the Happy Hours that we organize for the community occasionally.

host_about:
'Not all who wander are lost.' I love this quote. 
I am that wanderer, incredibly lucky to be infected with the passion and audacity to travel often and solo. 
I was born and raised in San Francisco. I am a native. I love my city. I’ve watched it evolve. But I have also left it many times in my youth. I’ve left it to study abroad in France. Best decision of my college life! I backpacked solo around western Europe. 
I’ve left SF when I was a member of the Armed Forces and was stationed around our country. I’ve also driven as far north as Niagara Falls and over to the Canadian side. 
Career wise, I’ve spent a decade working in property management and rentals. As a hobby, I write 90-minutes every morning at dawn, six-days a week. 
I am cursed with this blessing of being unceasingly interested in people. I love meeting people. I love hearing stories. And I love writing them. 
As I review my life’s experiences, I’ve come upon one very simple realization, that proclaimed secret of success. It is merely this: ‘Say what you will do and do what you will say.’
The prolific Seth Godin, talented blogger said creativity isn’t the most important part. What counts is being able to ship! Ship on time. And ship again. And again. And again.

The San Remo Hotel is conveniently located along the 49-Mile Scenic Drive in a quiet historic San Francisco North Beach neighborhood.

North Beach is a neighborhood in northeast San Francisco adjacent to Chinatown, Fisherman’s Wharf and Russian Hill. The neighborhood is San Francisco’s Little Italy, and has historically been home to a large Italian American population and is still home to many Italian restaurants. Today, North Beach is populated by a mix of young urban professionals, families and Chinese immigrants connected to adjacent Chinatown. The American Planning Association has named North Beach as one of ten ‘Great Neighborhoods in America’.

Fisherman’s Wharf and Pier 39 beckon to the north, only a few intersections away. A half-mile south, the lofty twin spires of Saints Peter and Paul Church are visible high above rooftops, marking Washington Square, the heart of North Beach. neighborhood_overview:
Historical Telegraph Hill
Now: The iconic Coit Tower is the focal point of the area for most visitors, but if you're willing to take your time and wander (and hike a couple of steep stretches of steps) you can catch a lot of extra scenery. Many people take the Greenwich Street steps since they are closest to the tower, and return the same way. The Filbert Street steps, just to the south, lead through much more of the lush landscaping characteristic of Telegraph Hill. Our neighborhood is also known for supporting a flock of feral parrots, primarily red-masked parakeets (Aratinga erythrogenys), descended from escaped or released pets. The flock was popularized by a book and subsequent documentary (2003), both titled The Wild Parrots of Telegraph Hill.

Then: The name Telegraph Hill came from a structure built on the top of the hill in the mid-1800s, which would visually signal the city with regard to the type of vessels passing through the Golden Gate.

It is perhaps the most colorful swath of acreage in San Francisco, and remains one of the last-standing neighborhoods to retain an eccentric personality.

The Haight rose to fame during the Counterculture Movement during the Vietnam War era; it became a regular feature in international news headlines and incited a global initiative for social change with special thanks to the 1967 Summer of Love, and a little help from Janis Joplin and the Grateful Dead.

The Haight-Ashbury neighborhood is nestled in between three parks: Golden Gate Park, the Panhandle, and Buena Vista Park, making it somewhat of an urban oasis. Within the parks you'll find: Museums, botanical gardens, seasonal music festivals, and a tea garden.

neighborhood_overview:
The Haight Ashbury was developed in the 1880s and 1890s, and many of the original buildings remain today from 'working class' Victorians such as our home to grand mansions that have been lovingly restored and maintained.

Free professionally led walking tours of the the historic Haight Ashbury are offered several Sundays each month.

This is a great walking area with shopping on Haight Street less than two blocks away. Golden Gate Park with its green expanses and Sunday carfree days, is minutes away, Both the de Young Museum, and the California Academy of Sciences in Golden Gate are an easy 20 minute walk away.

There are bike rental shops on Haight Street and along the borders of the GG Park. In addition the city sponsors a bike share program where one can rent a bike in one location, and drop it off in another location.
host_about:
John is American born (Dallas), but raised in the Washington DC area. Fell in love with California while attending graduate school at UCLA. After 3 years abroad - 1 year advanced studies in Bordeaux France and 2 years teaching at the University of the Witwatersrand in Johannesburg South Africa, he returned to California and has lived in San Francisco since 1974. He founded The Wine House, a wine import, wholesale, and retail business in San Francisco in 1977, which allowed him to combine his love of travel & interest in other cultures into a career centered on bringing people together through the pleasures of wine & food around the table.

neighborhood_overview:
Haight-Ashbury is an incredible relic of San Francisco’s past. The neighborhood, also known as “The Haight” or “Upper Haight”, succinctly personifies the City’s history, aesthetic, and culture.

It is perhaps the most colorful swath of acreage in San Francisco, and remains one of the last-standing neighborhoods to retain an eccentric personality.

The Haight rose to fame during the Counterculture Movement during the Vietnam War era; it became a regular feature in international news headlines and incited a global initiative for social change with special thanks to the 1967 Summer of Love, and a little help from Janis Joplin and the Grateful Dead.

The Haight-Ashbury neighborhood is nestled in between three parks: Golden Gate Park, the Panhandle, and Buena Vista Park, making it somewhat of an urban oasis. Within the parks you'll find: Museums, botanical gardens, seasonal music festivals, and a tea garden.

host_about:
I love to travel and fell in love with San Francisco on a trip and just had to move here!  I'm so happy and proud to be a San Franciscan!  I love sharing the city's beautiful landscape, neighborhoods and culture with first-time visitors and long-term residents alike.  

My family and I own several apartments that we have restored with love and care.  Our furnished apartments are always rented out long-term.  When we have a short gap between renters, we occasionally are able to offer a unit on Airbnb. Perhaps the greatest blessing of all is good health and I’m grateful for that as well.  I’ve been told by so many people that I have more energy than anyone they’ve ever known that there must be some truth to it. In my entire life, I have very rarely been sick – even a common cold. It’s my belief this amazing gift of health and energy – of life – could be given to everyone in the world in equal measure to what I have received.  It’s my belief that this gift carries with it the responsibility to give my best to those I serve, and to make the world a better place.

name: Dorm Beds at Social SF Hostel #12
description:
Our social and vibrant hostel in downtown SF is the place to stay! Each dorm room has 4-8 single beds. We focus on creating a community vibe that encourages guests to gather together, share a meal and exchange travel stories!

The space
Each room has 4-8 single beds, bunk bed style. There are five single occupancy bathrooms on each floor, each with complimentary essential oil organic lavender shampoo, conditioner, and shower gel. We also have a free sauna on the top floor and massage chairs in the lobby for your every relaxation need.
Our Grand Ballroom is the heart of the hostel where people play music, make friends and unforgettable memories, fall in love with the city and each other, and raise glasses in celebration. The ballroom, where musicians are always invited to play, has a pool table, ping pong table, books, games, and complimentary coffee and tea throughout the day. We provide free wi-fi throughout the hostel and also free computer use in our inter
neighborhood_overview: Our hostel is located in the culturally rich neighborhood of North Beach (SF’s Little Italy) and borders America’s largest Chinatown. We have great food and great fun on all sides! The rhythm of the Beat poets flow in the streets outside their regular hangouts, like Vesuvio, and City Lights Bookstore, just a couple of blocks away. And we are only a 20 minute walk from the famous Fisherman’s Wharf.
host_about:
There's one word that fully encompasses the experience of staying at our hostel: Community. At first glance, one might presume that the endgame of all hostels is to create a sense of firm familiarity among guest and staff alike, but with us, you can feel it. With a full roster of events that are ongoing, all inclusive in both experience and price, and a design purposefully conducive to the gathering of folks all around the world, we are dedicated to establishing a world reaching community that you feel while you are here, and long after your stay.

Our adventure travel company launched in 1974 with the purpose of bringing together folks who share the same single ambition: Travel! For the next twenty years, our buses brought these wandering souls to experience places as close as Santa Barbara and Monterey, to destinations as far as Alaska, New York City, and even Costa Rica. As incredible as these destinations are, we believe it is more about the journey than the destination.  

In the 1990’s we opened our San Francisco hostel to offer a haven for travelers to settle, rest, and of course party! In opening our hostel, we hoped to create a sense of community and create a haven where these newly found friendships would flourish.  We believe that bringing people together to create a community is the true purpose of a hostel.

Community. That’s what we’re about.  Stop by and experience it for yourself.

The Haight rose to fame during the Counterculture Movement during the Vietnam War era; it became a regular feature in international news headlines and incited a global initiative for social change with special thanks to the 1967 Summer of Love, and a little help from Janis Joplin and the Grateful Dead.

neighborhood_overview:
The Potrero Hill district is one of the most unique neighborhoods in San Francisco and has gone through several changes from working class to the newer family oriented direction since the 1990's

Potrero Hill is one of the sunniest neighborhoods in San Francisco. It is insulated from our famous fog and chill from the ocean and gives some of the most spectacular views of downtown and the bay bridge. If you are up for a few hills it can be a great walking experience and the ever growing "hub" of 18th street is always a great place to start a day.

One of the best parts of Potrero Hill is that it is a neighborhood further from the "hustle and bustle" so it has a quiet and sleepy feel but you are never more than a few minutes from the fray.
host_about:
We are working professionals whom love this city and takes a lot of pride in showing people how great a place it is.  We love world traveling, enjoying other cultures and meeting new people.

We are big movie buffs, foodies to our core and can't live without some good coffee :) 

Giving new people an opportunity to experience San Francisco is what we hope to do as hosts.  One of us was born in San Francisco (the other in Miami) and think there are a ton of fantastic things to experience here while on your stay either for work or fun :)

We hope that people have a fun and relaxing stay but mostly are happy!

neighborhood_overview:
Haight-Ashbury is an incredible relic of San Francisco’s past. The neighborhood, also known as “The Haight” or “Upper Haight”, succinctly personifies the City’s history, aesthetic, and culture.

It is perhaps the most colorful swath of acreage in San Francisco, and remains one of the last-standing neighborhoods to retain an eccentric personality.

The Haight rose to fame during the Counterculture Movement during the Vietnam War era; it became a regular feature in international news headlines and incited a global initiative for social change with special thanks to the 1967 Summer of Love, and a little help from Janis Joplin and the Grateful Dead.

The Haight-Ashbury neighborhood is nestled in between three parks: Golden Gate Park, the Panhandle, and Buena Vista Park, making it somewhat of an urban oasis. Within the parks you'll find: Museums, botanical gardens, seasonal music festivals, and a tea garden.

host_about:
'Not all who wander are lost.' I love this quote. 
I am that wanderer, incredibly lucky to be infected with the passion and audacity to travel often and solo. 
I was born and raised in San Francisco. I am a native. I love my city. I’ve watched it evolve. But I have also left it many times in my youth. I’ve left it to study abroad in France. Best decision of my college life! I backpacked solo around western Europe. 
I’ve left SF when I was a member of the Armed Forces and was stationed around our country. I’ve also driven as far north as Niagara Falls and over to the Canadian side. 
Career wise, I’ve spent a decade working in property management and rentals. As a hobby, I write 90-minutes every morning at dawn, six-days a week. 
I am cursed with this blessing of being unceasingly interested in people. I love meeting people. I love hearing stories. And I love writing them. 
As I review my life’s experiences, I’ve come upon one very simple realization, that proclaimed secret of success. It is merely this: ‘Say what you will do and do what you will say.’
The prolific Seth Godin, talented blogger said creativity isn’t the most important part. What counts is being able to ship! Ship on time. And ship again. And again. And again.

host_about:
It’s been said that knowing what someone is grateful for and the challenges they’ve overcome tells you a lot about them. For me there’s nothing in my life that I am more grateful for than my three adult sons who were also my life’s greatest challenge to raise as a single mother in San Francisco.  
In the crucible of parenthood, I have learned so much about working with people and developed qualities that are enormously beneficial in the world of work. When you have children whose lives depend on you, there’s no such thing as “I can’t” or “I’m tired” or “I couldn’t make it happen because…” Year in and year out, in life’s longest marathon, it became a deeply engrained habit to give my best every day and make it happen. 
 Being the sole responsible person for three growing boys required discipline, patience, diplomacy, negotiating skills, selflessness, tenacity, compassion, tenderness, endurance, resourcefulness, toughness and, last but not least, a thick skin. These same qualities are the foundation that has allowed me to succeed as an Executive Assistant for top executives at some stimulating and interesting companies, including early stage, privately held, and household-name corporations.  
Perhaps the greatest blessing of all is good health and I’m grateful for that as well.  I’ve been told by so many people that I have more energy than anyone they’ve ever known that there must be some truth to it. In my entire life, I have very rarely been sick – even a common cold. It’s my belief this amazing gift of health and energy – of life – could be given to everyone in the world in equal measure to what I have received.  It’s my belief that this gift carries with it the responsibility to give my best to those I serve, and to make the world a better place.

The oldest building in San Francisco is here. Founded in 1776, Mission Dolores still stands at 16th Street and Dolores, and is open to visitors as well as those attending its services. description:
Large stylish bedroom in a lovely three bedroom modern apartment in the Mission District. Walking distance to Valencia Street , BART, 24th Street and the numerous shops, cafes and restaurants the Mission has to offer.
This bedroom has a nice queen bed, a large closet and chest of drawers so there's plenty of storage room for your clothes and belongings. The bathroom is of a modern minimalist design and very well appointed with a large tiled shower.

The space
The apartment occupies the top floor of a lovely period Victorian house. The entire space has been beautifully remodeled. As you can see in the photos it has a large open plan kitchen and living room that lead out onto an elevated deck overlooking an oasis of urban backyards.
This is a great location, right in the heart of the Mission and an excellent launching pad to wherever you'll want to go in San Francisco.

description:
Spend your time in San Francisco living in a classic Victorian apartment, with bright rooms and an amazing view of Twin Peaks and the Mission District. The unit has been recently updated with a fresh coat of paint, new floors and new beds and bedding.

The apartment is bright and clean, and is located on a quiet residential street. There is plenty of parking in the area and easy access to two different bus lines that will take you to downtown San Francisco.

The space
I have lived in the house for over 14 years, I live in the apartment above the unit, and I never get tired of the great weather, the private street or the beauty of a Victorian home built in 1890. The downstairs apartment is a completely separate unit with a private entrance. It has 2 bedrooms, a large kitchen and a living room. There is also a balcony with a killer view of the Mission and Twin Peaks. The unit is also able to access a private garden with a place to sit and a fire pit.

 Being the sole responsible person for three growing boys required discipline, patience, diplomacy, negotiating skills, selflessness, tenacity, compassion, tenderness, endurance, resourcefulness, toughness and, last but not least, a thick skin. These same qualities are the foundation that has allowed me to succeed as an Executive Assistant for top executives at some stimulating and interesting companies, including early stage, privately held, and household-name corporations.  
Perhaps the greatest blessing of all is good health and I’m grateful for that as well.  I’ve been told by so many people that I have more energy than anyone they’ve ever known that there must be some truth to it. In my entire life, I have very rarely been sick – even a common cold. It’s my belief this amazing gift of health and energy – of life – could be given to everyone in the world in equal measure to what I have received.  It’s my belief that this gift carries with it the responsibility to give my best to those I serve, and to make the world a better place.

description:
Eden is a shared hostel bedroom with half bathroom located in the historic Red Victorian, near Haight-Ashbury. This listing is for the single bed pictured, intended for one guest.

The Red Victorian is an experimental community run hotel that offers unique guest experiences. While here, we invite you to attend events: lectures & talks, skill shares, music nights, art shows!

Near Golden Gate Park and Twin Peaks, this central location also offers easy direct lines to both downtown and the beach.

The space
This single bed is the first one found inside Eden, a huge beautiful well-lit room. Located on the top floor, Eden is the sunniest room in the house and filled with light and plants. The room is also the quietest room in the house (furthest from the street), and is located directly across from the cozy third floor lounge. It has its own private bathroom. It used to be the room that Sami Sunchild (the Red Victorian’s founder) once occupied.
neighborhood_overview:
Haight-Ashbury is an incredible relic of San Francisco’s past. The neighborhood, also known as “The Haight” or “Upper Haight”, succinctly personifies the City’s history, aesthetic, and culture.

It is perhaps the most colorful swath of acreage in San Francisco, and remains one of the last-standing neighborhoods to retain an eccentric personality.

The Haight rose to fame during the Counterculture Movement during the Vietnam War era; it became a regular feature in international news headlines and incited a global initiative for social change with special thanks to the 1967 Summer of Love, and a little help from Janis Joplin and the Grateful Dead.

The Haight-Ashbury neighborhood is nestled in between three parks: Golden Gate Park, the Panhandle, and Buena Vista Park, making it somewhat of an urban oasis. Within the parks you'll find: Museums, botanical gardens, seasonal music festivals, and a tea garden.

neighborhood_overview:
Music City Hotel is located in the vibrant Polk Gulch/Lower Nob Hill neighborhood. Immediately to the left when exiting the Hotel is Polk Street, filled with a wide array of incredible food options, shops, as well as unique bars and nightlife. The neighborhood has historical significance as the original center for San Francisco’s LGBT community and more recently has harbored members of the arts community and important music venues such as Kimo’s, Great American Music Hall, The Regency Ballroom, The Masonic Theater, and more.

In the 1960s at the height of the counterculture movement, a music venue in the neighborhood called The Avalon Ballroom played a vital role in hosting influential acts such as Moby Grape, Quicksilver Messenger Service, and the Grateful Dead. Fast forward to today, and the Polk Gulch has maintained its local charm of both new, modern and long-standing businesses that serve both the neighborhood and beyond.

name: L'hotel Excelsior!
description:
The room is comfortable for 4 people. A group of 7 told me they slept great. It gets cramped. It gets stuffy. There is 1 bathroom to share. 4 is plenty but, if you insist, I won't say no. I will, however, charge extra for each night an additional guest stays. I want happy guests.

90% of my guests arrive from other countries. I want to avoid misunderstandings so now I insist that guests CONTACT me BEFORE requesting a reservation.

And about PARKING? NO! NADDA! ZERO! ZIPPO! ZILCH!

The space
I think my listing is unique because it provides relative privacy with the benefit of living with locals who are happy to offer tips and tricks about getting around and what to see as well as thoughtful insight and an insider's perspective of the city. I am very proud to provide my guests with the best map of the city: The official MUNI transit map! They are only sold in a few locations and I make a special trip to purchase these maps for my guests.
neighborhood_overview:
I live in a neighborhood called The Excelsior. 100+ years-ago it was a semi-rural suburb of San Francisco, now it is a culturally diverse family neighborhood. Ironically, the streets were named, un-ironically, and in no particular order, for cities and countries in Europe and Asia.

Beautiful views of the city can be had from McLaren Park - within easy walking distance from my doorstep.

To me, the neighborhood is a respite from the hustle and bustle of the denser parts of the city.
host_about:
Unemployed Efficiency Architect. 

For the last few years I have been laboring as an overworked agent of chaos. Recently, I have turned a corner; I can see a quiet order as I focus on gratitude and acceptance. Chaos is not a lifestyle; chaos is a test of strength and perception. If you survive the storm you are obligated to make something out of the broken mess left behind. A new architecture. a new system. a new point of view. efficiency is relative.

host_about:
Our secluded property, once a large thoroughbred horse and black angus ranch has been in my family for over 40 years. It reflects my husband's and my two passions: wine and horses. We  breed and race thoroughbred horses and each spring just about the time new buds form on the grape vines, new foals are born.
The guesthouse is a rambling ranch style home with racing memorabilia, antiques, a large commercial style kitchen, wonderful views, decks, vegetable garden and pool area.  We are an established Bed and Breakfast. We have been hosting guests here for more than 27 years. We have met wonderful people who have become great friends. Most people who stay here have an adventuresome spirit. They come here seeking an authentic experience in the wine country. Our remote ranch  is surrounded by forest, hills and vineyards and is a natural, quiet and private setting. 
Jim and I along with our four dogs, fourteen cats and sixteen horses invite you to experience our unique lifestyle, enjoy great wines and unwind in our idyllic environment.

neighborhood_overview: The Precita Park area of Bernal Heights is a safe neighborhood with a great corner market and three fantastic restaurants.  Locals say we live in the "Banana Belt", meaning we often get sunshine when the rest of the city is wrapped in fog.  From our house, you can walk two blocks down to Precita Park and two blocks up to Bernal Hill Open Space for a great 360 degree view of the San Francisco Bay Area.  Take a short walk through the eclectic streets of Bernal to three distinct neighborhood commercial areas:  the Mission, Cortland Ave, and La Lengua where you will find great restaurants, cafes, shops and markets.
host_about:
Kelli and I live with our three tuxedo cats in the Bernal Heights neighborhood of San Francisco.  I work as a public school teacher for students with special needs, and Kelli is a landscape architect with San Francisco's Recreation and Parks.  We love to share our home, garden and neighborhood with friends and family from around the state, the country and the world. Our community of Manchester Commons consists of our home, our friends' home next door and a shared garden between the two.   All of us at Manchester Commons enjoy welcoming new people to San Francisco.  

     Kelli and I have lived in a few American cities before settling in San Francisco, and we enjoy meeting new people from near and far.  I may be biased when I say our neighborhood is the best in San Francisco, but it's actually true:-)  We love to share our favorite things with guests (see our Guide Book).  Among many other gems in the neighborhood, there are two beautiful public parks;  a variety of terrific restaurants, cafes, and bars and an amazing brewery; there are quintessential San Francisco walks to be had in and around Bernal Hill, and our neighborhood is close to so many other wonderful neighborhoods--the Mission District, Dogpatch, Noe Valley, the Castro, and Glen Park.  The transportation options are great with multiple buses, bike share and the 24th St BART station about a 10 minutes walk. 

     We also love to travel!  Our favorite recent trips include our family cabin in the Sierra Nevada Mountains; friends and family in New York City and Los Angeles; London, Berlin, Barcelona, Croatia, and Japan.  I spent a year abroad living and studying in Sweden, traveling throughout Scandinavia and Northern Europe.  We both love learning from different cultures and people.

host_about:
'Not all who wander are lost.' I love this quote. 
I am that wanderer, incredibly lucky to be infected with the passion and audacity to travel often and solo. 
I was born and raised in San Francisco. I am a native. I love my city. I’ve watched it evolve. But I have also left it many times in my youth. I’ve left it to study abroad in France. Best decision of my college life! I backpacked solo around western Europe. 
I’ve left SF when I was a member of the Armed Forces and was stationed around our country. I’ve also driven as far north as Niagara Falls and over to the Canadian side. 
Career wise, I’ve spent a decade working in property management and rentals. As a hobby, I write 90-minutes every morning at dawn, six-days a week. 
I am cursed with this blessing of being unceasingly interested in people. I love meeting people. I love hearing stories. And I love writing them. 
As I review my life’s experiences, I’ve come upon one very simple realization, that proclaimed secret of success. It is merely this: ‘Say what you will do and do what you will say.’

I am cursed with this blessing of being unceasingly interested in people. I love meeting people. I love hearing stories. And I love writing them. 
As I review my life’s experiences, I’ve come upon one very simple realization, that proclaimed secret of success. It is merely this: ‘Say what you will do and do what you will say.’

host_about:
Greetings from Noelle and George!

We both grew up in the Bay Area and are college sweethearts having both majored in biological sciences. We chose to live and raise a family which includes our three children in San Francisco because of the beautiful landscape, amazing culture and diversity, priceless climate and lets not forget exploring this beautiful city through the iconic cable car rides.

As a family we enjoy spending most of our time outdoors which includes hiking in the Marin Headlands, breezy walks along Ocean Beach, as well as biking in Golden Gate Park to name a few. Camping is a major part of our summer routine in Lake Tahoe, Yosemite National Park, and Camp Mendocino. We also enjoy Lake Tahoe during the winter months for skiing and snowboarding. Noelle and I are also avid sports fans and LOVE attending San Francisco Giants, Oakland Athletics, Golden State Warriors, San Francisco Forty Niners, Oakland Raiders and San Jose Shark games with our children and friends. Our weekends are also consumed with youth sports as our children play on baseball, basketball, golf, and swimming teams.

 We are lucky enough to live in an area which embraces the arts and we are just a short stroll away from the many music festivals which San Francisco has to offer and a few of our favorite events to attend are the Blue Grass Festival and Outside Lands both in Golden Gate Park. 

San Francisco offers a variety of multi-cultural cuisine all within a short distance from each other whether it be a walk, drive or door step away. Some of our favorites include, fresh seafood, Pho, Mission-style burritos, Korean BBQ, Cioppino, or exploring our palates with tasting world renowned wine and cheese at the Ferry Building!

My kid's favorite playground!

This natural area with a valley & lake also offers trails & a wide range of migratory birds.

It consists of several park sections including the Concert Meadow, the West Meadow, and Pine Lake Park. The grove's Pine Lake is one of three natural lakes in the city of San Francisco. host_about:
'Not all who wander are lost.' I love this quote. 
I am that wanderer, incredibly lucky to be infected with the passion and audacity to travel often and solo. 
I was born and raised in San Francisco. I am a native. I love my city. I’ve watched it evolve. But I have also left it many times in my youth. I’ve left it to study abroad in France. Best decision of my college life! I backpacked solo around western Europe. 
I’ve left SF when I was a member of the Armed Forces and was stationed around our country. I’ve also driven as far north as Niagara Falls and over to the Canadian side. 
Career wise, I’ve spent a decade working in property management and rentals. As a hobby, I write 90-minutes every morning at dawn, six-days a week. 
I am cursed with this blessing of being unceasingly interested in people. I love meeting people. I love hearing stories. And I love writing them. 
As I review my life’s experiences, I’ve come upon one very simple realization, that proclaimed secret of success. It is merely this: ‘Say what you will do and do what you will say.’
The prolific Seth Godin, talented blogger said creativity isn’t the most important part. What counts is being able to ship! Ship on time. And ship again. And again. And again.

host_about:
'Not all who wander are lost.' I love this quote. 
I am that wanderer, incredibly lucky to be infected with the passion and audacity to travel often and solo. 
I was born and raised in San Francisco. I am a native. I love my city. I’ve watched it evolve. But I have also left it many times in my youth. I’ve left it to study abroad in France. Best decision of my college life! I backpacked solo around western Europe. 
I’ve left SF when I was a member of the Armed Forces and was stationed around our country. I’ve also driven as far north as Niagara Falls and over to the Canadian side. 
Career wise, I’ve spent a decade working in property management and rentals. As a hobby, I write 90-minutes every morning at dawn, six-days a week. 
I am cursed with this blessing of being unceasingly interested in people. I love meeting people. I love hearing stories. And I love writing them. 
As I review my life’s experiences, I’ve come upon one very simple realization, that proclaimed secret of success. It is merely this: ‘Say what you will do and do what you will say.’
The prolific Seth Godin, talented blogger said creativity isn’t the most important part. What counts is being able to ship! Ship on time. And ship again. And again. And again.

host_about: Hi!  We are Tim and Lisa.  These are a few of our favorite things: Our adopted city of San Francisco (we've both lived here over 3 decades), our local neighborhood (the Richmond District), meeting people, nature (birds/beaches/hiking/etc.), live music (especially at SF's fantastic music venues, including the music festivals right here in Golden Gate Park), food, and our family (we have 2 adult daughters and 2 grandkids).  We met while teaching at the well-respected preschool that Tim co-founded in 1984.  Tim comes from a hotel/restaurant family (The Treadway Inns in New England), and now newly retired, he looks forward to returning to his family roots as a friendly and helpful host.  Tim loves to garden and cook. Lisa still happily teaches 2-, 3- and 4-year-olds (coming up on her 31st year at the same school).  Like Tim, she is also from the East Coast (NY).  We put tons of love, care, comfort and quality into building our new apartment, as we expect to live down there ourselves one day.  We currently live upstairs from the apartment and are therefore easy to contact if you need anything (our guests choose how much or little interaction to have with us).  Please let us know if you have any questions!

host_about:
'Not all who wander are lost.' I love this quote. 
I am that wanderer, incredibly lucky to be infected with the passion and audacity to travel often and solo. 
I was born and raised in San Francisco. I am a native. I love my city. I’ve watched it evolve. But I have also left it many times in my youth. I’ve left it to study abroad in France. Best decision of my college life! I backpacked solo around western Europe. 
I’ve left SF when I was a member of the Armed Forces and was stationed around our country. I’ve also driven as far north as Niagara Falls and over to the Canadian side. 
Career wise, I’ve spent a decade working in property management and rentals. As a hobby, I write 90-minutes every morning at dawn, six-days a week. 
I am cursed with this blessing of being unceasingly interested in people. I love meeting people. I love hearing stories. And I love writing them. 
As I review my life’s experiences, I’ve come upon one very simple realization, that proclaimed secret of success. It is merely this: ‘Say what you will do and do what you will say.’
The prolific Seth Godin, talented blogger said creativity isn’t the most important part. What counts is being able to ship! Ship on time. And ship again. And again. And again.

neighborhood_overview:
The Dogpatch is a hub for creatives with a wondrous industrial setting. The district was a simple shipbuilding district of San Francisco in the 1800s. Lots of the vintage grit still stands in the Dogpatch today, which can arguably be compared to the steampunk rage that’s been hitting the U.S. this generation.

This idyllic art and design district is also home to several foodie spots that are defining SF food culture. We recommend Piccino's for dinner and brunch (pasta!), Just for You Cafe for diiner food, Farley's or La Stazione for a cappuccino and cannoli, Neighbor Bakehouse for baked goods, Daily Driver for wood fired bagels, La Fromagerie for cheese and sandwiches, Oliver's Butchery for anything you want to grill, and basically any brewery or wine bar on 3rd (there are many!). Just up the hill, you can walk to Good Life Grocery for any basic needs.

Haight-Ashbury is an incredible relic of San Francisco’s past. The neighborhood, also known as “The Haight” or “Upper Haight”, succinctly personifies the City’s history, aesthetic, and culture.

It is perhaps the most colorful swath of acreage in San Francisco, and remains one of the last-standing neighborhoods to retain an eccentric personality.

The Haight rose to fame during the Counterculture Movement during the Vietnam War era; it became a regular feature in international news headlines and incited a global initiative for social change with special thanks to the 1967 Summer of Love, and a little help from Janis Joplin and the Grateful Dead.

The Haight-Ashbury neighborhood is nestled in between three parks: Golden Gate Park, the Panhandle, and Buena Vista Park, making it somewhat of an urban oasis. Within the parks you'll find: Museums, botanical gardens, seasonal music festivals, and a tea garden.

North Beach is a neighborhood in northeast San Francisco adjacent to Chinatown, Fisherman’s Wharf and Russian Hill. I am that wanderer, incredibly lucky to be infected with the passion and audacity to travel often and solo. 
I was born and raised in San Francisco. I am a native. I love my city. I’ve watched it evolve. But I have also left it many times in my youth. I’ve left it to study abroad in France. Best decision of my college life! I backpacked solo around western Europe. 
I’ve left SF when I was a member of the Armed Forces and was stationed around our country. I’ve also driven as far north as Niagara Falls and over to the Canadian side. 
Career wise, I’ve spent a decade working in property management and rentals. As a hobby, I write 90-minutes every morning at dawn, six-days a week. 
I am cursed with this blessing of being unceasingly interested in people. I love meeting people. I love hearing stories. And I love writing them. 
As I review my life’s experiences, I’ve come upon one very simple realization, that proclaimed secret of success. It is merely this: ‘Say what you will do and do what you will say.’
The prolific Seth Godin, talented blogger said creativity isn’t the most important part. What counts is being able to ship! Ship on time. And ship again. And again. And again.

The Southern San Francisco area referred to everything south and central along with the eastern bent of Mission Street and District. The neighborhood extends to its end at the county line. Over the years, as the southern end of San Francisco was developed, the city created Major neighborhoods & Districts within the area, and these were given names that appeared on city maps. These are: Bernal Heights, Ingleside, The Excelsior District, Visitacion Valley & The Bay View District. As the city grew, The Excelsior District was developed further, and it was split into even smaller sub-neighborhoods useful for Real Estate. host_about:
Hey there! I'm a full-time-traveler turned full-time-teacher. Hoping to meet some awesome people on my next trip and see what cool cafes there are to sit at in town. I'm a musician and an explorer, an author of songs and of software. I'm easily impassioned with physical and mental pursuits--I used to live by a rock gym, so I went climbing every day. Now I live by a squash gym, and I'm suddenly an obsessive squash player.

I live to learn and to be surprised by the world. I cook most of my food from scratch, and travel to learn about the world, about people, and myself. I've found that opening my eyes to the good in everyone is one of the most surprising and fulfilling things in life, so I do it every chance I get. Traveling gives me a lot of those opportunities.

host_about:
'Not all who wander are lost.' I love this quote. 
I am that wanderer, incredibly lucky to be infected with the passion and audacity to travel often and solo. 
I was born and raised in San Francisco. I am a native. I love my city. I’ve watched it evolve. But I have also left it many times in my youth. I’ve left it to study abroad in France. Best decision of my college life! I backpacked solo around western Europe. 
I’ve left SF when I was a member of the Armed Forces and was stationed around our country. I’ve also driven as far north as Niagara Falls and over to the Canadian side. 
Career wise, I’ve spent a decade working in property management and rentals. As a hobby, I write 90-minutes every morning at dawn, six-days a week. 
I am cursed with this blessing of being unceasingly interested in people. I love meeting people. I love hearing stories. And I love writing them. 
As I review my life’s experiences, I’ve come upon one very simple realization, that proclaimed secret of success. It is merely this: ‘Say what you will do and do what you will say.’
The prolific Seth Godin, talented blogger said creativity isn’t the most important part. What counts is being able to ship! Ship on time. And ship again. And again. And again.
